speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have noticed the swelling in your neck and if it is painful or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, is this swelling firm and fixed to the underlying tissues, or is it mobile and soft? I would also like to know if you have experienced any recent unintentional weight loss or changes in your bowel habits. REQUEST TEST: CT_Scan_Neck_and_Chest

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal and the mass is painless, could you describe the consistency of the swelling—is it soft and doughy, or firm and rubbery? Also, does the swelling change in size when you lie down versus when you are upright? REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Neck

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound suggests a cystic lesion, so I need to check for infection or other causes. Do you have any history of tuberculosis or contact with cats, and is there any redness or warmth over the swelling? REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration

speaker: Doctor
text: The FNA was normal, which makes infection or malignancy unlikely given the cystic nature. Is the swelling purely subcutaneous and mobile, or does it feel attached to the fascia? Does it have a central punctum or any history of draining foul-smelling material? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of colon cancer, I am concerned this could be a metastatic deposit despite the normal FNA. Do you have any other lumps or swellings elsewhere on your body, and have you noticed any changes in your skin texture over the mass? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Neck

speaker: Doctor
text: With the MRI also normal, let me examine the mass directly; does it feel soft and doughy, and can you push it back into the neck when you lie flat? This would suggest a lipoma or a hernia of the neck fascia.

speaker: Patient
text: Overall healthy appearance, no other complaints or symptoms noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the mass soft and doughy to the touch, and does it become less prominent when you lie down? I suspect this is a lipoma given the benign imaging and lack of systemic symptoms.
